speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, lower leg swelling, and weight loss. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the unintentional weight loss and bilateral leg swelling are concerning. Given your history of chronic bronchitis, have you noticed any recent shortness of breath, cough, or changes in your sputum? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests, Urinalysis, D-Dimer.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, Leukocyte count 8500/mm3, Platelet count 130,000/mm3; COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL: Serum Urea Nitrogen 23 mg/dL, Glucose 77 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL, Albumin 1.8 mg/dL, Total Cholesterol 475 mg/dL; LIVER FUNCTION TESTS: [NOT PROVIDED IN SOURCE DATA]; URINALYSIS: Blood Negative, Glucose Negative, Protein 4+, WBC 0–1/hpf, Fatty casts Numerous; D-DIMER: [NOT PROVIDED IN SOURCE DATA]

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome secondary to Amyloidosis (likely AL type given the history of chronic bronchitis/inflammation).

The lab results show severe hypoalbuminemia, heavy proteinuria with fatty casts, and significant hypercholesterolemia, which confirms nephrotic syndrome. The elevated creatinine indicates renal insufficiency. I will now request a Kidney Ultrasound to assess for structural changes and potentially an immunofixation electrophoresis to investigate for underlying amyloidosis.
